title: BA1/1122/2019 of CHANDRAPAL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
BA1 No.1122/19
Hon'ble R.C. Khulbe, J.
 Mr. SRS Gill, Advocate, for the applicant.
 Mr. Ravi Joshi, Brief Holder, for the State.
 Heard.
 Applicant Chandrapal, who is in judicial
custody in connection with Case Crime No.84 of
2019 under Sections 420 IPC & Section 3 of Price
Chit & Money Circulation Scheme (Banning) Act,
1978 and u/s 3 of the Uttaranchal Protection of
Interest of Depositors in Financial Establishment Act,
2005, registered at Police Station Transit Camp,
District U.S. Nagar, has sought his release on bail.
 Heard learned counsel for the parties.
 As per the FIR, co-accused Kunwar Pal Singh,
Roop Kishore, Prakash Singh and Naval Kishore
came to the informant who are Directors & Leaders
of G.L. Shine Company and they induced the
informant, that if the informant will invest money in
their company, they will double the money and
further induced him that if he connects other people
to the company, he will be given Rs.1500/- per
person as commission. The informant invested
Rs.30,000/-. It is further alleged that the informant
also got Smt. Suman Kumari, Mohd. Ali and Tartil in
the company who invested their money. After some
days, when the complainant went to get the benefit in
cash from the company, the persons, connected
therewith, refused to give his money back.
 It is argued that the present applicant
Chandrapal is not named in the FIR. Moreover, he is
simply a Class IV employee in the said company.
Neither he received any money from the informant
nor is he beneficiary of the money which has been
deposited by other persons, as alleged in the FIR.
 Learned State Counsel argued that the offence
is serious in nature but it is admitted that the present
applicant is not named in the FIR and he is only a
Class IV employee in the company.
 It appears that the applicant has not induced
the informant and even he did not receive any money,
either from the informant or from the persons, as
alleged in the FIR. He is simply a Class IV
employee in the company and he has no role
whatsoever in the company.

Without making any comment as to the final
merits of the case, the bail application is allowed. Let
the applicant Chandra Pal be enlarged on bail on
executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable
sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of
the Magistrate concerned.
 It is, however, clarified that these observations
are exclusively for the purpose of bail and the same
shall not affect the trial proceedings in any manner
whatsoever.
